text:
marie: heads-up — seeing sustained GPU pool saturation in eu-west-1 from ~09:10-09:35 UTC. The weird part is 60% of queued requests are streaming chat sessions but they account for ~85% of tail latency and KV cache pressure.
aj: confirmed, I can repro on the dashboard. Streaming requests hold KV slots much longer (avg 9s) vs sync (avg 0.7s). Queues fill and batch jobs starve.
ben: are these mixed-priority tenants or mostly same tier? cost/plan?
marie: mostly hosted free+standard tiers hitting same model forks. Not a single tenant issue. Looks like admission treats streaming and sync equivalently right now.
olga: for some workloads streaming is the only UX option (token-by-token). But if streaming floods the pool we should degrade gracefully.
dave: short-term mitigation: lower streaming concurrency at edge for eu-west and route some streams to dedicated fallback pool. Long-term: we need admission weights + preemption.
marie: Agreed. Proposal: separate realtime vs batch queues, then admission control uses dynamic weights based on headroom and cost. Quick config idea:
```
admission:
  realtime_queue_weight: 0.6
  batch_queue_weight: 0.4
  preempt_streaming_after_ms: 12000
  max_concurrent_streams_per_node: 4
```
ben: i worry preemption for streaming is trickier — we'd need graceful truncation or fallback to truncated chunks, otherwise apps break. Also cost: moving to dedicated pools for some tenants increases bill.
aj: operationally we can implement a soft preempt: when preempted, send a short-system-event to client and switch to async-delivery. That keeps connection but drops immediate tokens.
olga: we must keep SLOs for realtime customers. Maybe tier-based weights: enterprise streams get protected quota, free streams are best-effort.
dave: +1 on tiered quotas. Also add a per-region capacity threshold that flips to conservative mode: when gpu_util > 85% for 5m, shift weights to favor short sync jobs by 2x.
marie: can we do a quick experiment? lower max_concurrent_streams_per_node to 3 for eu-west and enable the conservative-weight flip at 85% for 30m canary. Monitor queue depth, p99 latency, evicted KV hits.
ben: i can patch the runtime admission flags in staging and run a canary in eu-west canary cluster.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/admission-flags @ben -> staging/eng-runtime-canary at 1806004360.
aj: running telemetry watchers now. If p99 drops and batch throughput recovers we consider rolling to prod with a gradual ramp.
marie: note: also add a metric for "kv-slot-hold-time" by request-type so we can quantify streaming vs sync impact over time.
olga: also add an alert: if queued_streams > 250 for 2m => page oncall. We've been missing that threshold before.
dave: one more thought — investigate lightweight token-batching for streaming tails (bundle small trailing tokens across sessions) to reduce kernel invocations. Research/ML can test quantization impact too.
marie: thanks. action items: ben patch + canary, aj observe, olga draft tiered quota policy, dave research batch-for-tails, marie will own metrics/alert. Back in 30m with results. :hourglass:
